persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from directory_1843, newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “John Ludby” (f1839_v0497, printed page 44, ward 4, voting for John H. Kinzie). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Ludby' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins J. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 4 times, as “LUDBY JOHN”, 1834-10-16 to 1834-12-27: 3 federal land entries — SE sec 32 T40N R14E; W2NEVOID sec 20 T39N R14E; W2NW sec 32 T39N R14E, 320.00 acres stated in all, for $400.00 (ls0428, ls0480, ls0562, ls0563). The register states this purchaser's residence as COOK, so the sale is contemporary evidence that a man of this name lived in Cook County on the date of sale. It is not evidence that he lived in the town. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: LUDBY JOHN matches John Ludby: the forename names John Ludby of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. merge_ruling.for_merge: A terminal y lost, 'John' identical, and 'Ludb' is set NOWHERE in the deposited corpus while Ludby is set three times — the profile of a truncated reading rather than a family. John Ludby is a documented man: Fergus 1843 has 'Ludby, John, soap and candle maker, South Branch, 3 miles south [died January 24, 1872, aged 78.]', and the Democrat prints him on 19 November 1834.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS NEVER TOUCH. 'John Ludb' is the post-office return of 2 July 1834 (#c029) and nothing else; John Ludby is the Democrat of 19 November 1834 (#c006) and Fergus 1843 — a letter list against a newspaper and a directory, D7's own example. No issue and no return is caught setting both spellings, and the letter-list card is not an anchor: T-0482 closed it no_corroboration. The fold is admissible in shape and has no demonstration behind it, which is exactly what D7 is for. `for_merge` is kept because a later reading of the 2 July 1834 return's image could show the terminal y in the impression and close this.

occupation_later.note: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 prints this trade against this person, in the entry quoted on the card: 'Ludby, John, soap and candle maker, South Branch, 3 miles south [died January 24, 1872, aged 78.]'. It is evidence about 1843, written here as 1843's and read back onto no 1835 claim. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.
